content.title: Jalen Green leads Suns past Warriors, defending champion OKC next
content.text: Updated April 17, 2026, 10:05 p.m. MTJalen Green scored 36 points in leading the Phoenix Suns past the Golden State Warriors, 111-96, in the Play-In Tournament finale on Friday, April 17, before a sellout crowd of 17,071 at Mortgage Matchup Center.Green matched a career-high for made 3s with eight on 14 attempts.Earning the eighth seed, the Suns will next face the defending NBA champion and No. 1 seed Oklahoma City Thunder in the first round of the Western Conference playoffs. Game 1 is Sunday, April 19, at 12:30 p.m. MST, at Paycom Center in Oklahoma City. The game will be televised on ABC.Phoenix went 2-3 against the Thunder in the regular season.This was Green’s first game against the Warriors this season after missing the four regular-season matchups due to injury. The Suns went 1-3 in those games.This was the first time Green faced Golden State since last season’s playoffs while playing for the Houston Rockets. The Warriors upset the No. 2 seeded Rockets in the first round.This time, Green got the best of the Warriors in leading the Suns to victory to advance to the playoffs after missing postseason play last season.Devin Booker added 20 points and Jordan Goodwin 19 in the win.The Suns limited Stephen Curry to 17 points.The Suns were without Mark Williams (left foot soreness). Grayson Allen (left hamstring strain) was available, but didn't play. 3rd Q: Suns 78, Warriors 69Jalen Green had 27 points, going 7-of-12 from 3, in leading the Phoenix Suns to a 78-69 lead going into the fourth quarter.Green’s career-high for made 3s is eight, as he matched it last month against the Toronto Raptors.The Suns have 22 points off 15 Golden State turnovers.Stephen Curry had just 13 points through the 3rd, on 3-of-10 shooting, going 0-for-4 from 3. 2nd Q: Suns 50, Warriors 45 at halfGolden State cut Phoenix's 18-point lead down to two points before Jalen Green's late 3 over Al Horford put the Suns ahead, 50-45, at the half.The Warriors outscored the Suns, 30-17, in the second quarter as they only committed three turnovers in the quarter that led to just four Phoenix points.The Suns scored 13 points off nine Warriors' turnovers in the first quarter.Jalen Green has a game-high 14 points after going for 35 in Tuesday's loss to the Portland Trail Blazers in the 7-8 Play-In Tournament game at Mortgage Matchup Center.Brandin Podziemski leads the Warriors with 12 points. Stephen Curry has just seven points on 2-of-16 shooting in 16 minutes.Curry scored 27 of his 35 points in the second half of Golden State's 126-121 comeback win Wednesday over the Los Angeles Clippers in the 9-10 Play-In game in Inglewood.The Warriors-Suns winner will earn the eighth seed in the Western Conference playoffs and face defending NBA champion Oklahoma City Thunder in the first round, starting with Game 1 on April 19 in Oklahoma City. 1st Q: Suns 33, Warriors 15The Phoenix Suns scored 13 points off nine Golden State turnovers in taking a 33-15 lead at the end of the first quarter.All five starters scored for the Suns as Dillon Brooks accounted for eight points. He also picked up two fouls in the first quarter.Stephen Curry only took two shots in the first quarter, scoring just two points.The Suns shot 6-of-15 from 3 while the Warriors went 1-of-9. Suns plan to play 'bigger wings' vs WarriorsThe Phoenix Suns will be without Mark Williams (left foot soreness), but Grayson Allen (left hamstring strain) is available for tonight's Play-In Tournament game against the Golden State Warriors.The Suns are starting Devin Booker, Jalen Green, Jordan Goodwin, Dillon Brooks and Oso Ighodaro in place of Williams.Suns coach Jordan Ott talked about playing "bigger wings" against the Warriors, a move that can be interpreted as giving players like Ryan Dunn, Haywood Highsmith, rookie Rasheer Fleming and Amir Coffey some minutes.Dunn played nine minutes in Tuesday's loss while Highsmith, Fleming and Coffey didn't play as Ott shrunk down his rotation to nine."All hands on deck," Ott said pregame. "We've been figuring it out on the fly all season long. Got to do it again tonight. We're small in general. When we go smaller, we just have to play our bigger wings and find a way to protect the paint and these guys, they shoot as many 3s as anyone else in the league. Got to do our best to take that way and offensively, continue to play faster than even what we have recently. We've got to get into the open court, use our speed and skill since we won't have as much size."The Warriors are starting Stephen Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Gui Santos, Draymond Green and Kristaps Porzingis (right ankle soreness), who has been upgraded from questionable to available.Have opinions about the current state of the Suns?
